- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% if recent 3–5 days show downward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in the following 5–10 days; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 1–3% from forecast for next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is near recent mean, model often fails to mean-revert; use 3–5 day moving average of past 10–15 days as baseline for correction.
- For horizon >14 days, model tends to overestimate in bullish sentiment periods; apply a “decay factor” (e.g., multiply forecast by 0.95–0.98) if sentiment >0.67 over last 7 days.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., -0.33 or below) and price is rising, model may misread trend; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days to avoid “sentiment reversal” bias.
